question: A 22-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 2-week history of cough and decreased urination. The cough was initially nonproductive, but in the last few days he has coughed up small amounts of blood-tinged sputum with clots. He has not had any fevers, chills, or weight loss. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 5 years. Pulse is 115/min and blood pressure is 125/66 mm Hg. Physical examination shows dried blood around the lips. Serum studies show a creatinine of 2.9 mg/dL. Results of a serum antineutrophil cytoplasm antibody test are negative. A biopsy specimen of the kidney is most likely to show which of the following light microscopy findings?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Smoking -> lung damage -> cough with blood-tinged sputum -> 70% CHAIN: Smoking -> renal damage -> decreased urination -> 60% CHAIN: Renal damage -> elevated creatinine -> 80% CHAIN: Elevated creatinine -> kidney biopsy -> light microscopy findings -> 70% CHAIN: Light microscopy findings -> fibrin crescents in Bowman space -> 70%
analysis: The clinical presentation of a 22-year-old man with cough, hemoptysis, decreased urination, elevated creatinine, and negative ANCA test is suggestive of Goodpasture syndrome, an autoimmune disease affecting the kidneys and lungs. In Goodpasture syndrome, there is an autoimmune attack on the basement membrane of the glomeruli and alveoli, leading to glomerulonephritis and pulmonary hemorrhage.
